observations: User reports battery at 4.0 V and main rail at correct 3.3 V.
With USB only, /dev/cu.usbmodem101 enumerates and status command responds.
User attached battery, unplugged USB and reconnected USB while battery remained attached.
After this reconnect, /dev/cu.usbmodem101 remained absent and ioreg showed no USB JTAG/serial debug device.
User pressed RESET with battery and USB still attached. USB device reappeared and status responded; Wi-Fi connected, NFC initialized.
User then followed BOOT+RESET download-mode entry and unplugged/reconnected USB with battery attached.
Host observed USB disappear/reappear during button sequence, then disappear during unplug; no device reappeared after user confirmed reconnect.
ROM download-mode entry was not independently confirmed by protocol before the second reconnect. Treat this as a control attempt, not proof of ROM operation.
On battery power alone, user measured VBUS remaining at 2.1 V with RESET released and dropping almost to 0 V when RESET is pressed.
confirmed_workaround: After reconnecting USB with battery attached, briefly press RESET (BOOT released). Verified once.
source_findings: Native USB D-/D+ use GPIO18/19, USBLC6 protection U4 and 22-ohm R12/R13.
VBUS sensing Q2 drives active-low USB_PRESENT_N to GPIO1; Nucula firmware does not currently consume this signal.
No application deep/light sleep calls or USB pin reassignment found.
Console sends with portMAX_DELAY. Potential offline blocking is separate from host-level device disappearance.
conclusion: Confirmed reset-dependent backfeed onto connector VBUS from the battery-powered board. Rev-A wiring, U4 topology, RESET-dependent VBUS collapse, and host power-on during RESET strongly identify ESP32 USB D+ pull-up -> R13 -> U4 upper steering diode -> VBUS as the cause of failed USB-C attachment. The particular U4 current path is inferred with high confidence, not physically isolated.
changes: Diagnostic report updated only; no firmware, flash, NVS or schematic changes made.
host_log_findings: 17:07:35: cable-change power-on and successful enumeration, coinciding with user RESET recovery.
17:09:15: cable-change power-off and device removal; no subsequent power-on/enum recorded before log capture despite confirmed cable reconnection.

hypotheses.status: high-confidence circuit diagnosis; reset-dependent VBUS backfeed measured
hypotheses.description: The battery-powered ESP32 USB D+ pull-up feeds connector VBUS through the U4 USBLC6-2SC6 upper steering diode. VBUS stays at 2.1 V, preventing the USB-C source from reaching its required safe-zero attach condition. RESET removes the source of the backfeed, allowing VBUS to fall and the host to attach.
support: U4 pin 5 is connected to raw VBUS in rev-A netlist.
USBLC6-2 manufacturer documents a rail-to-rail protection topology.
USB-C source attach requires VBUS at vSafe0V.
Host cable-power-on occurs during RESET recovery.
User measured C14 VBUS at 2.1 V and C12 ESP_EN at 3.3 V with USB and battery connected in the failed state.
Battery-only VBUS is 2.1 V with RESET released and nearly 0 V with RESET held; USB cable is disconnected during these measurements.
limits: U4 has not been electrically isolated and D+ has not been measured; the exact diode current path remains an inference.
Board 3.3 V was not simultaneously captured during RESET; no oscilloscope power transient measurements made.

future_fix_requirements: Prevent the battery-powered USB data lines from energizing connector VBUS; review data-line ESD topology and retain suitable ESD protection for data and VBUS.
Implement valid VBUS-dependent USB attachment. Review Q2 sensing at the measured 2.1 V before relying on USB_PRESENT_N for a firmware-only workaround.
Validate battery-only VBUS discharge and repeated battery-powered USB-C reconnects after any fix; include ROM download-mode recovery.
